categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Fraud Allegations, Token Price Concerns, and Developer Activity

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members expressed frustration over the token reaching new all-time lows with no official communication from the team. One user noted a single-day drop of over 12 percent with no response from the project. A user named Bangrrr raised serious fraud allegations, claiming that the Eliza Foundation used approximately 750,000 CAD of investor funds to invest in a public shell company called Secure Blockchain Development Corp, which then returned those funds back to Eliza under the guise of a B2B revenue contract. The user cited public SEDAR filings, a Fasken Law Firm press release dated April 10, 2026, and an active New York Southern District Court class action lawsuit (Case 1:26-cv-03238) naming Sebastian Quinn-Watson, a director of the acquired company Agentic Solutions, as a core defendant. The user described this as round-tripping, a deceptive accounting practice used to fabricate organic enterprise adoption. Other community members, particularly J_CHOY, repeatedly challenged the allegations and demanded direct evidence be posted in the channel, dismissing the claims as hearsay. Another user pointed out that the declining token price itself serves as evidence of underlying problems. A separate user named Arunsajeev from human.tech asked for technical support regarding a merged registry pull request for a third-party plugin that was not appearing in the agent settings. A new community member named Fabio also introduced himself, highlighting his background in AI, full-stack development, machine learning, and agent-based systems.

In the coders channel, a builder behind a project called RPC Edge announced a free alpha program for Solana traders and bot teams, offering access to performance-focused RPC infrastructure, Yellowstone gRPC, and transaction sending services in exchange for feedback on latency and reliability. A developer named Solify expressed interest in ElizaOS and noted over eight years of experience in blockchain, full-stack, and AI development, looking to collaborate. An unrelated political image was posted by a user named Peter. A link to an external post on X was also shared by Kim Diaz.

In the general discussion channel, community members exchanged brief greetings. Users stg_trey, Othman, and Admiin each posted short hello messages in the evening hours, indicating light social activity in the server.

In the coders channel, a developer named Ginga posted a message asking if anyone was looking to hire a developer. Later, Omid Sa replied to a separate conversation suggesting that contributors could solve open issues on the main ElizaOS GitHub repository as a way to get involved.
In the partners channel, user Burtiik posted a brief affirmative response, though the context of the original conversation was not available in the provided data.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Developer Activity

content.text: On July 17, 2026, the ElizaOS community discussion channel saw a handful of brief interactions. A community call for a project called Zeroclaw was announced and taking place, with at least one member asking to join. One user expressed skepticism about the future of ElizaOS, stating that not even Justin Sun could save it. A developer posted asking if anyone was looking to hire a developer. Activity in the coders channel was minimal, consisting of a single emoji reply between two members.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Token Sentiment

content.text: In the ElizaOS Discord discussion channel, a brief conversation took place on July 18, 2026 regarding the future of the ElizaOS token. One user expressed a bearish outlook, claiming that exchanges would delist the token within two months followed by a significant price decline. Another user pushed back on this sentiment, acknowledging that while the tokenomics may not look ideal, elizaOS is actively building and developing meaningful products. A third user reacted to the exchange with amusement. The coders channel had no activity recorded for the same date.

categories.title: Scam Activity and Security Warnings in Community Channels

content.text: On July 19, 2026, a user identified as MR james posted identical messages across both the general discussion channel and the coders channel, claiming to have made $31,000 from rugging meme coins and offering to teach others how to conduct rug pulls. The user solicited direct messages from interested parties, framing the offer as free help. This activity was flagged as a scam. In the discussion channel, a community helper known as THE UNDERRATED MAJ warned another user, El_Lince, not to click any scam support links, not to accept direct messages from unknown users, and to report anyone who sends unsolicited DMs. The warnings received positive reactions from community members. Separately, El_Lince had asked why the updates channel was not working, which appeared to be unrelated to the scam activity. The channel topic for the coders channel directs users to the official ElizaOS documentation at docs.elizaos.ai for getting started with agent development.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Activity and Project Status

content.text: Community members in the discussion channel expressed concern about the apparent inactivity of the ElizaOS project and its Discord server. One member noted that the only visible signs of life from the community are GitHub updates, and suggested monitoring the elizaos-github Discord channel for activity. Speculation arose that the silence may be related to ongoing legal proceedings or a deliberate decision to stay quiet until an anticipated app release. Members also noted that communication has been declining despite previous promises, and even spam activity in the channel has ceased. A developer posted asking if anyone was looking to hire, suggesting some community members remain engaged despite the low activity.
